# Skid plate selection and fabrication

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Prioritize the radiator and gas tank skids, noting the latter's plastic construction. [t179]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Prioritize the radiator skid as it is crucial for protecting engine components.
2. Rank the gas tank next due to its vulnerability and potential cost of damage.
3. Consider the engine, transmission, and transfer case skids lower in importance since obstacles can often be seen and adjusted around.

_Procedure reported by [t179]._

## Parts

- [Partial] Gas tank skid: High priority, protects plastic fuel tank [t179]
- Radiator skid: Crucial for protection [t179]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Note that the 2nd gen gas tank is made of plastic. [t179]
- Full steel skids change how you wheel by reducing concern for belly scraping. [t179]
